correctness.rationale: For a>=2, a short leaf cannot host a stack of size >=3: its only length-three exits reach long-arm ends and force a stack >=4, larger than the eccentricity-three target can ever receive. Each short leaf must therefore send its initial cup to the center or receive the center single cup. Two leaves cannot both clear: two incoming cups immobilize the center, while an outgoing center move empties it forever. For a=1 the four target orbits have exact move words; the outer-end construction has verified even/odd index rules and consumes each original vertex exactly once. BFS-distance replay of 476 positive orbit cases b=2..120, and full state enumeration of nine negative finite cases, both pass. Unbounded correctness comes from these symbolic arguments, not interpolation.

value.rationale: This gives an exact infinite-parameter classification for the natural shortest unresolved mixed-arm spider family in a recent graph stacking game: a single short arm is compatible with all targets, but any second short arm prevents stacking onto all length-two-arm inner vertices. The positive side supplies explicit linear-length winning algorithms, including distinct odd and even routing mechanisms to distant arm ends. This is not a routine bound or a numerical table.
